post.summary: Send a sign-in code to a WhatsApp number
post.description: Only a Pakistani mobile number (`+923` and nine digits) gets a code: any other number is validation_failed with `{ path: "phone", code: "phone_not_pakistan_mobile" }`, before anything is counted or sent. Sign-in limits replace the `auth_code` bucket: code requests and code checks are limited per number and per client address, each number gets at most 10 codes a day, and codes for the whole country have hourly and daily ceilings; refresh is limited per client address. Every limit answers `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds` (and a `Retry-After` header). The numbers are API settings, not part of the contract.

post.summary: Record a day read (reader, goal met, "I read today" or the session portion)
post.description: One row per person, Pakistan-time date and source; sending it again is safe and changes nothing but the totals. `pages` and `ayahs` are the day's totals so far for that source (not increments): a repeat keeps the larger of the stored and the sent value. `date` defaults to today in Pakistan; only today and yesterday are accepted, anything else is validation_failed with `{ path: "date", code: "out_of_range" }`. `attendance` cannot be sent: the server records it when a coordinator marks the person present by name. The first day read of a date adds one to the national readers total, and new pages add to the national pages total, counted without the user id. Returns the whole day, all sources together. Only the person can read their days; coordinators and admins cannot.

get.summary: Own days read between two dates
get.description: Inclusive Pakistan-time dates, at most 366 days. A backwards range is validation_failed with `{ path: "from", code: "invalid_range" }`, a longer one `{ path: "to", code: "too_big" }`. Days without any reading are left out, in date order. There is no streak: the app counts days, for example "4 of 7 days this week".

get.summary: The ayah of the day: surah and ayah numbers only
get.description: Rule (`resolveDailyAyah`): when exactly one pick of a followed venue or circle applies that day, that pick; otherwise the national pick; otherwise the built-in list (`BUILT_IN_DAILY_AYAHS`). Send the ids of the venues and circles the person follows as repeated `venueId` and `circleId` parameters; a signed-out visitor sends none. `date` defaults to today in Pakistan. No text is returned: the reader shows the Arabic and the translation from its own source.

get.summary: Registrants of a session in scope, with names and numbers
CSV export of registrants of a session in scope
CSV export of registrants for a city or venue, with dates, in one call
get.description: One audited export for what the person asked for, instead of one per session. Filters: `cityId`, `venueId`, and `from` / `to` (inclusive local dates, Pakistan time, of the registration). The caller must hold `registration.export` for every venue the file covers; a filter outside their scope is `forbidden`. With no filter a coordinator gets their whole scope. A `cityId` or `venueId` that does not exist is `not_found` for a caller who holds `registration.export` anywhere (the rule for unknown ids in a request); someone with no export right at all gets `forbidden` and learns nothing. More than 50000 rows is refused with validation_failed and the issue code `too_many_rows`: narrow the filters. The file is UTF-8 without a byte order mark (the console adds one when it saves) and its header row is exactly: session_id,venue_id,city_id,name,phone,party_size,section,status,registered_at. Cells that start with '=', '+', '-', '@' or a tab in names are prefixed with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas. One audit row records the filters and the row count, never the cells. `registrations.export` (one session) is unchanged.

An unknown venue or circle is `not_found`. Surah and ayah numbers only (the ayah must exist in the surah), never text. One audit row per change.

key.description: Lower case letters, digits, - and _; at most 40

post.summary: Make posters for a session: one queued poster per format
post.description: Checked with `poster.create` at the session's venue. The server builds the snapshot from the session as it is now (`posterSnapshotFromSession`, `sessionVersion` = the session's `updatedAt`), inserts one `posters` row per format with `status: 'queued'`, and enqueues one `poster-render` job (`PosterRenderJob`) for them. Editors type the title and details only: the date, time and venue come from the session, so a poster cannot disagree with it. A title is required in every language the poster shows (`{ path: "fields.title.ur", code: "custom" }`). An unknown or inactive `templateKey` is `not_found`, by the rule for unknown references; a format the template does not offer is validation_failed with `{ path: "formats", code: "invalid_value" }`. While a poster for the same session and template is still `queued` (any format or language, a remake included), a new one is `conflict`: wait for it, then regenerate if needed. A queued poster older than an hour no longer blocks. `adminPosters.create` and `adminPosters.regenerate` share a per-staff allowance (10 a minute by default, an API setting) on top of the default bucket; over it, `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`. Answers 202 with the queued rows; poll `adminPosters.list` until they are `ready` or `failed`.

templateKey.description: Lower case letters, digits, - and _; at most 40
Lower case letters, digits, - and _; at most 40

get.summary: Posters of a session, with status, file and whether each is out of date
get.description: Checked with `poster.read` at the session's venue. Newest first. `outOfDate` compares each poster's `sourceSnapshot` with the session now (`posterOutOfDate`): `{ reasons: ['time'] }` when the time, days, timezone or one-off date changed, `'venue'` when the venue, its name or its area changed, null while it still matches. The console and the admin app show the out-of-date band and a Regenerate action from it. `fileUrl` is set once a poster is `ready`; `failureCode` once it has `failed`.

templateKey.description: Lower case letters, digits, - and _; at most 40

post.summary: Make a poster again from the session as it is now
post.description: Checked with `poster.create` at the poster's session's venue. Same template, language, format and fields; a fresh snapshot; a new queued row with `replacesPosterId` set, and a `poster-render` job for it. The old poster stays until the new one is ready, then it is deleted with its file (by the worker). A poster that is still `queued` cannot be regenerated yet: `conflict`. `adminPosters.create` and `adminPosters.regenerate` share a per-staff allowance (10 a minute by default, an API setting) on top of the default bucket; over it, `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`. Answers 202 with the new row.

get.summary: Download a ready poster: a PNG or a PDF
get.description: Checked with `poster.read` at the poster's session's venue. Answers the stored bytes with `Content-Type: image/png` (story, link preview) or `application/pdf` (A4, A3) and `Content-Disposition: attachment` with a file name. A poster that is not `ready` has no file yet: `conflict`.

post.summary: Invite a coordinator by phone number. Checked by the role in the body
post.description: Sends the invitation message and keeps a pending invite. To resend, send a new invite for the same number, role and place: it replaces the pending one with a fresh expiry and sends the message again (there is no separate resend call). To hand a city or venue to someone with no account yet, add `replacesAssignmentId`: the replaced assignment is revoked at once, and the invite stays pending until the new assignment is created on acceptance. The returned `Invite` (and each item of `adminRoles.invites`) carries `replacesAssignmentId`, so a resend can copy it. A resend of a pending handover invite keeps the handover even without it, while the replaced assignment is still live; a `replacesAssignmentId` that is unknown, ended or at another place is `not_found`. Each person may create a limited number of invites in any 24 hours, counting single invites, resends and imports together (an API setting, 200 by default): over it, validation_failed with `{ path: "phone", code: "invite_daily_limit" }` and nothing is sent.

post.summary: Import venues from a file: dry run, or all or nothing
post.description: Rows are `VenueCreate`. Needs `venue.create` for each row's city; a row outside the caller's scope is invalid with the issue code `forbidden`. A venue with the same city and English name that already exists, or an earlier row with the same city and name in the same request, is `duplicate` (skipped, not an error). With `dryRun: true` every row is checked and nothing changes. With `dryRun: false` all rows are written in one transaction, or none if any row is invalid (`applied` says which). A file that clashes with a write made by someone else between the check and the write is refused as a whole with `conflict` and nothing is written; send it again (rows already there come back as `duplicate`). One audit row records the row counts, never cell contents. Retrying a file is safe: rows that were already imported come back as `duplicate`.

rows.description: Up to 2000 rows. Each row has the shape of the single create call for venues, and is validated one by one; a malformed row is reported as invalid in the result.

post.summary: Invite many coordinators from a file: dry run, or all or nothing
post.description: Rows are `InviteBody`. Each row is checked with the action for its role (`role.assign_*`), exactly as `adminRoles.invite`; a row the caller may not invite is invalid with the issue code `forbidden`. A pending invite for the same number, role and place, or a person who already holds that role there, is `duplicate` (skipped, not an error). With `dryRun: true` every row is checked and nothing changes. With `dryRun: false` all invites are created in one transaction, or none if any row is invalid, and the invitation messages are queued only after it commits. A file that clashes with a write made by someone else between the check and the write is refused as a whole with `conflict` and nothing is written; send it again (rows already there come back as `duplicate`). One audit row records the row counts, never phone numbers. Retrying a file is safe: rows that were already imported come back as `duplicate`. Two ceilings refuse the whole file, dry run included, with validation_failed and no result (`IMPORT_REQUEST_ISSUE_CODES`): more than 100 rows is `{ path: "rows", code: "too_big" }`; rows that would take the caller past their invitations for the last 24 hours (as for `adminRoles.invite`; duplicate and invalid rows do not count) is `{ path: "rows", code: "invite_daily_limit" }`.

rows.description: Up to 2000 rows. Each row has the shape of the single create call for coordinators, and is validated one by one; a malformed row is reported as invalid in the result.

post.summary: Import sessions from a file: dry run, or all or nothing
post.description: Rows are `SessionCreate`. Needs `session.create` for each row's venue; a row outside the caller's scope is invalid with the issue code `forbidden`. A session at the same venue with the same English title, kind, start time and days (or date), or an earlier identical row in the same request, is `duplicate` (skipped, not an error). A recurring row whose `endsOn` is before its `startsOn` is invalid with the issue code `invalid_range`. With `dryRun: true` every row is checked and nothing changes. With `dryRun: false` all sessions and their occurrences are written in one transaction, or none if any row is invalid. A file that clashes with a write made by someone else between the check and the write is refused as a whole with `conflict` and nothing is written; send it again (rows already there come back as `duplicate`). One audit row records the row counts, never cell contents. Retrying a file is safe: rows that were already imported come back as `duplicate`.

rows.description: Up to 2000 rows. Each row has the shape of the single create call for sessions, and is validated one by one; a malformed row is reported as invalid in the result.
